title: Revenue that never caught up
lede: Every figure here comes from the company’s annual reports on EDGAR. The 2000 and 2002 reports give five years each, and they agree where they overlap. Prices are adjusted for the two-for-one split of May 1999, so the $9 offering price appears as $4.50.

blocks.title: Revenue and net loss, 1996–2002
blocks.subtitle: $ millions, by calendar year.

points.title: the IPO year
points.text: Revenue of $5.5M and a loss of $16.0M.[^7]

points.title: the worst year
points.text: A $103.9M loss, $68.6M (derived) of it restructuring, impairment and goodwill amortization.[^7]

points.title: the switch-off
points.text: The community closed in August 2001; revenue fell to $16.1M.[^11]

points.title: a magazine company
points.text: $9.7M of revenue, mostly Computer Games magazine and Chips & Bits.[^11]

blocks.source: Annual reports for 2000[^7] and 2002[^11]. Net loss is shown as a positive number. Rounded from thousands.
